reviews.reason: The candidate commit only makes quantity affect `total`; the delivery/free-delivery computation was left untouched and still sums bare `item.price` without quantity. Static evaluation of `delivery([{price:10,quantity:3}])` yields `10 >= 30 ? 0 : 5` → `5`, while the acceptance test expects `0`, which exactly matches the host-run failure `5 !== 0` on both the Builder tree and the clean committed tree. Because `total([{price:10,quantity:3}]) === 30`, the regression test is not skipped; it fails. Two of three acceptance tests pass (quantity total, checkout button visible), but the free-delivery success criterion is unmet, so the candidate must be rejected.
evidence: checkout.mjs:1 — `total` now applies quantity: `sum + item.price * (item.quantity ?? 1)` (passes functional test at tests/acceptance.test.mjs:6)
checkout.mjs:2 — `delivery` unchanged: `sum + item.price` ignores quantity; for the fixture `[{price:10,quantity:3}]` it computes 10, returns 5, but the test expects 0
tests/acceptance.test.mjs:5-8 — fixture `{ price: 10, quantity: 3 }`; line 8 asserts `delivery(items) === 0`; skip branch is not taken since `total(items) === 30`
style.css:1 — `.checkout { padding: 16px; }` removed `display: none`, satisfying tests/acceptance.test.mjs:7 (checkout button visible)
Host evidence, Builder tree and clean committed tree: `✖ regression: free delivery after correct total ... 5 !== 0` (test-0-637b029f..., test-0-59517120...) — consistent with static derivation above
blockingRisks: Failing acceptance test `regression: free delivery after correct total` (1 of 3 failing) on the committed tree — success criteria require all acceptance tests to pass.
Delivery threshold semantics are internally inconsistent: `total` is quantity-aware but `delivery` is not, so an order whose true subtotal reaches 30 is still charged 5.

findings.description: `delivery` in checkout.mjs must compute the same quantity-aware subtotal as `total` (e.g. `items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.price * (item.quantity ?? 1), 0) >= 30 ? 0 : 5`) so orders with subtotal ≥ 30 receive free delivery; currently it sums `item.price` only, yielding 5 for `[{price:10,quantity:3}]` and failing tests/acceptance.test.mjs:8.

Inconsistent quantity handling between the two exported functions is the root defect; the candidate fixed the reported total bug but not the dependent delivery calculation, leaving the success criterion 'Orders with subtotal at least 30 receive free delivery' unsatisfied.
